text:
maria: FYI — enterprise customer Acero reported sudden p95/p99 spikes on text-generation calls since last night. They saw p95 jump ~3x and p99 occasionally >10s. Customer claims this started after our infra rollout at 02:10 UTC (driver + kernel updates). Request IDs: r-8a2f, r-8a33, r-8a44. Can we triage?

devon: Ack. Which fleet/region? Any pattern (model, seq len, route)?

maria: Hosted eu-west-1, model redwood-lite-7b, typical seq len 512. Affects both streaming and non-stream. Only on dedicated/gpu-backed hosts AFAICT. No change in customer prompt behavior.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] SLO breach candidate: .p99_latency > 6s for route /v1/generate (eu-west-1). Link: https://console.redwood/slo/incidents/1755009999 :rotating_light:

ashley: Is there a rollout timeline? I remember kernel + driver rolled through eu-west between 01:50-02:30. I pushed an infra note at 02:35. Might be correlated.

sam: Can we get iostat and nvme stats from affected hosts? Check queue depth and latency. Run on host: `iostat -x 1 10` and `nvme telemetry get-log /dev/nvme0 --log-id=0x04`. Also share `dmesg | tail -n 200`.

maria: Collecting logs now. Running iostat + dmesg on node gpu-eu-047. Will paste snippets shortly.

devon: Also grab runtime traces + token timestamps for one slow request. Use `X-Request-ID: r-8a33` example. If we can get per-token delta from runtime that helps isolate KV cache/driver stalls.

maria: Paste from iostat (short):
```
avg-cpu:  5.0 us,  1.2 sy,  0.0 ni, 93.8 id,  0.0 wa
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         120.5   10.4  10240.0  512.0     86.4     0.66  12.58  0.21   12.58  0.25  30.1
```

maria: dmesg shows repeated timeouts and reset on nvme for that node.

jin: That avgqu-sz 0.66 + await 12ms is suspicious under our load. Could be host kernel IO scheduler differences with new kernel. Did the rollout change qdisc or blk-mq settings?

sam: Affirmative — we applied a kernel patch that adjusted `nr_requests` and blk-mq depth defaults. Might interact poorly with our high-concurrency NVMe pattern. Rolling back those kernel flags on one canary node is probably quickest repro.

devon: Meanwhile, can we apply an immediate mitigation at runtime? Options: reduce max_concurrency per-device, lower batch sizes, or fall back to CPU variant for the failing pool. Which is lowest-risk?

ashley: Reduce concurrency and batch size on the affected dedicated pool for the customer. That should reduce NVMe queue pressure. Also enable KV cache warmup/longer TTL to avoid cold KVs hitting disk.

maria: I've applied a 30% concurrency cap for Acero on gpu-eu pool and forced smaller batch_size=4 for their route. Monitoring now.

ops-bot: [ACTION] Deployment change: concurrency cap applied to pool "gpu-eu-dedicated" for customer Acero. ID: act-1755010321

maria: After cap: p95 dropped from ~3.6s -> ~1.4s within 5 minutes. p99 still has occasional tails at ~6-8s.

devon: Good. Let's still capture perf counters from the GPU (nvml) and check if kernel or driver is stalling GPU threads. `nvidia-smi -q -d UTILIZATION` and `sudo perf record -a -g -F 99 -- sleep 10` on the node during a slow request.

maria: nvml shows 80-95% GPU util but occasional complete stalls for 200-400ms aligned with NVMe resets in dmesg.

jin: That alignment suggests driver/firmware bug where NVMe resets are blocking kernel workqueues that the GPU runtime depends on. We need to escalate to infra team and consider rolling back the kernel change in eu-west.

sam: I'll spin a canary rollback for kernel flags on two hosts in the pool and mark them as test. If those hosts show stable p99, we can do a broader rollback. ETA 12-20 mins.

devon: Also add a temporary routing policy: route Acero traffic away from hosts that show nvme resets. We have heuristics in smart-router — can we flip to avoid nodes with dmesg errors?

ashley: Yes, I'll update routing to avoid nodes with nvme errors and exclude them from scheduling. Done.

ops-bot: [STATUS] Routing rule updated. Rule ID: rr-1755011200. Excluding 3 hosts from scheduling.

maria: Canary rollback applied to gpu-eu-053 and gpu-eu-054; early numbers: p99 on those hosts ~1.2s, no nvme reset in dmesg.

devon: Good repro and clear signal. Plan: 1) Rollback kernel flags region-wide in eu-west (sam) 2) Keep concurrency cap and routing rule for Acero until rollback completes (maria/ashley) 3) Open vendor support ticket with NVMe/driver vendor including dmesg, nvme telemetry, and perf traces (jin) 4) Postmortem once stable. Agree?

sam: Agree. I'll start rollback + coord with SRE.

jin: I'll gather logs + file vendor SR. Include `nvme error log`, `dmesg`, `iostat`, `nvidia-smi` traces and timestamps around r-8a2f/r-8a33.

maria: Noted. Customer update sent: we applied temporary cap and routing; working on rollback. Next update in 30m.

devon: After rollback completes, let's run a controlled repro: run a 30m load test using same model/seqlen against both patched and rolled-back hosts and compare p95/p99 and NVMe metrics. Use `vegeta` or our internal load-runner and include token-level latency traces.

ashley: I'll schedule that and document the experiment in the incident board.

ops-bot: [REMINDER] Incident owners: sam (infra), jin (eng-ml), devon (runtime), maria (CS). SLA breach status: under review.

maria: Update at +45m — rollback is in progress; p95/p99 across region trending down. Keeping this thread active.

devon: Once stable, we should add a kernel/driver compatibility test to CI that simulates our NVMe access pattern. Prevents regressions when we bump kernel/drivers next time.

maria: Agreed. I'll include that in postmortem actions.

ops-bot: [CLOSE-EVAL] Monitoring for 2 hours. If no regressions, we'll transition to postmortem.
